overview: After 2...d4 White plays 3.Rg1 aiming for g4-g5 and a quick kingside pawn push, giving up castling. Black can simply develop with ...c5 and ...Nc6, or hit g4 with ...h6 and ...Nc6. It is a rare joke-like variation and I read it only from the moves.

white_ideas.idea: Advance g4, g5 and h4 against the king
Fianchetto the bishop and play e3 to challenge d4

black_ideas.idea: Use the space on d4 and counter on the queenside

typical_structures.structure: Benoni-like with Black pawn on d4 and White kingside pawn advance

character.notes: White gives up castling rights, rich in risk.

character.reason: An early kingside pawn storm with an unsafe king.

soundness.reason: Losing castling rights for a pawn storm is questionable.

structure.reason: The pawn on d4 is attacked and the centre is undecided.

plans.reason: White pushes the g- and h-pawns.
